messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier these days—more whispers, more glances, but no one’s stepping forward yet. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are deeper than they seem, and no one knows which way they’ll split first."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier, but the cracks are still just whispers—no one’s sure if the walls are shaking or if we’re just listening too closely. Keep your circles warm, but don’t mistake quiet for calm; the jokes are sharper now, and that’s how it starts."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering slowly, but the clouds haven’t broken yet. The regime’s grip is tightening in some ways, loosening in others, and the cracks are showing, but no one’s sure who—or what—will come through them first."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken yet—just more clouds gathering. The regime’s grip is tighter, but the cracks are in the small things: delays, whispers, and the way even the loyalists seem to be holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like the first quiet before a storm. The usual rules seem looser, but trust only what you see with your own eyes. Stay sharp, stay safe, and keep your circle tight."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels heavier this month—like the weight before a storm, not the calm after. The usual signs are there, but the timing is still unclear. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. We’ll know soon enough which way the wind blows."*"
Sender 7: "*"The trees are still standing, but the wind is shifting—quietly, without warning. Best to keep your roots deep and your branches light."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken yet—just more clouds gathering. Keep your eyes open, your plans flexible, and your words measured; the wind could shift in any direction."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the wind’s holding its breath. The usual cracks are still there, but the walls are being reinforced, not repaired. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather seems calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer is twitching. The old roof still holds, and the neighbors are keeping up appearances, but even the most careful among us are quietly checking their raincoats. Let’s stay ready, not restless."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different now—like the tide is turning, even if no one’s sure exactly when the wave will break. Keep your eyes open, but your words light. The streets are whispering what the regime’s exercises can’t hide."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels lighter—small cracks are showing, but the walls still stand. Keep your steps quiet, your eyes open, and your plans ready, but not yet set in stone."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather forecast is changing—clouds gathering, but the wind is shifting too. Best to check your rain gear and share the news quietly with those who’ll understand."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—hot one minute, cold the next—but the old walls still stand. The gardeners are working harder than ever, and the neighbors have stopped complaining, even if they don’t know why. Best to keep tending our own plots quietly for now."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather’s been unpredictable lately—some days the wind shifts sharply, other days it’s eerily still. Best to keep your coats close and your boots ready, just in case. The old map might still be useful, but I’ve heard whispers that some of the roads are being rerouted without warning. Stay sharp, and let’s talk soon—quietly."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—some are sharpening knives, others packing bags, but no one’s sure which way the wind will blow. The walls still stand, but the cracks are widening, and the guards are watching each other as much as the streets. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—patience may be the only edge we have left."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather’s still unpredictable—some say the storm’s passing, others that it’s just gathering strength. The streets are quiet, but the air feels heavier, like everyone’s holding their breath. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans flexible—no need to rush, but no time to relax either."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering, but no one’s sure if it’ll break or pass. The usual rules seem quieter, and even the merchants are packing their bags early. Stay sharp, but keep your hands steady."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually warm for this time of year, but the forecasts keep changing. My cousin’s been too busy to call, and the neighbors are all talking about the same odd storms on the horizon. The government’s putting up new signs to explain it all, but even the birds seem restless. Let’s keep an eye on the sky."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather’s changing—even the birds are singing differently. The old walls are cracking, but no one’s sure yet if it’s the wind or the roots pushing through. Stay sharp, but keep your tools quiet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—old voices are stirring, but the regime’s grip is still tight, just less steady. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake tension for weakness; the game isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather looks steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting in ways that might mean a longer season ahead. Best to keep the garden tended and the tools sharp, just in case."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—some say it’s just a passing storm, but the wind’s shifting in ways we haven’t seen before. Best to keep an eye on the horizon and make sure your boots are sturdy, just in case."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier, but the ground hasn’t shifted yet—just more cracks in the pavement than last week. Keep your steps steady, your eyes open, and your circles small. The regime’s voice is louder, but the silence between its words is what matters now."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually calm, but the air feels heavy, like before a storm. Best to keep your rain gear close and your plans simple, just in case. No need to rush, but don’t be caught unprepared either."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
